analysis.title: The Ghosts Of Crises Past To Haunt The Midterms: Natixis Says A Democratic Sweep Could Exorcise The AI Bond Bear
key_insights: Natixis' Americas team (Berber, Hodge, Briggs, Aker) says the AI crowding-out story that pushed US real yields higher all year may have run its course. A Democratic sweep in Tuesday's midterms could take air out of it.

Natixis had the highest 10Y yield forecast on the Street for 2026 at 4.60%, built on the AI crowding-out thesis. It turned neutral on the long end earlier this month, 'admittedly 25bps before the peak', and now prefers to buy dips in a 4.90%-5.25% expected 10Y range rather than sell rallies.

The mechanism for a Democratic win is regulatory pressure and attention on AI buildout, not spending. AI capex only needs to not accelerate for bonds to benefit, so issuance and lending could come in below market expectations. Natixis expects no major federal legislation because Trump holds the veto pen and favors the AI buildout. It also says there will be no immediate rally since the agenda takes shape into 2027.

10Y real yields are around 2.7%, matching the 2007 highs and approaching the late-2008 spike (read from a chart). Natixis says real yields have returned to early-2000s levels 'and more', potentially overshooting.

The FOMC held at an upper bound of 4.00% after September's hike, with two hawkish dissents from Cook and Hammack. Natixis sees a December hike as 'now likely a foregone conclusion' absent a big data shift or substantial tightening of financial conditions.

Warsh plans to keep eight meetings a year but dedicate at least one exclusively to strategy, with no vote and no statement. Natixis does not think one fewer decision meeting means one fewer chance to hike.
Headline PCE rose 0.5% m/m and 3.6% y/y. Core PCE rose 0.3% m/m and 3.1% y/y. After a cool summer the last two prints have been noticeably hotter.

The personal savings rate fell to 3.8%, the lowest since October 2022. The Conference Board index rose 7.5 points to 91.7 in October on lower gasoline prices, but gas is still up more than 34% on the year and consumers plan to spend less on durables and services.

October payrolls are due Friday. Consensus is 55K with unemployment at 4.2%, after September's 29K, which was below all estimates. Across 2025 and 2026 only one payrolls print (March 2026) has exceeded the pre-pandemic average.

Midterm setup: Trump approval is about 38%. Since WW2 the president's party has lost an average of 25 House seats. Polymarket has Democrats at 94% for the House. The Senate is harder: Democrats must hold 9 safe, 3 likely and 3 lean seats and win at least two of five swing states (Texas, Kansas, Ohio, Iowa, Maine).

Front-end trade: Natixis keeps its 2Y long put on at about 4.88%, targeting 4.40%. With 2Y at about 4.60% the trade is up 28bps. It is trailing its stop down from 5.04% to 4.86%, and watches a rising weekly trendline at 4.48% next week.

Natixis expects Wednesday's refunding to bring 'little of note', with unchanged auction sizes and a message of flexibility. Citi expects Bessent to cut 20Y and 30Y auction sizes and possibly end the 20Y, because AI is taking the pension bid.

LatAm: Lula won Brazil's election with 51.79% of the vote. In a pre-election Natixis survey 76% of clients named fiscal responsibility as their main concern. Brazil fell 13.9% in a day, per the ZeroHedge October recap.

Chile's central bank warned that inflation risks have increased markedly, but Natixis gives the hawkish tone little weight. Growth is near zero and unemployment rose from 8.5% in January to 9.4%. Natixis expects rate hikes probably not until H2 2027.
Colombia: Natixis expects BanRep to pause with low conviction, then make a final December hike to 12.50%. The three-month annualized economic activity index is -13.2% and inflation is above 6%.

ZeroHedge commentary (not Natixis): the author agrees with the direction but thinks the bigger threat to AI issuance is the market itself, citing the AI funding window, Alphabet's worst day ever, Amazon's $33.5 billion cash burn and Intel's record crash. These sent the 10Y to a six-week low on Friday. If the funding window stays shut, the long end gets relief regardless of the election.

sector_views.rationale: Natixis frames AI capex as the driver of higher real yields via crowding out. It sees regulatory attention after a Democratic sweep as a possible headwind to capex growth, which would ease issuance pressure on Treasuries.

earnings_insights: ZeroHedge commentary cites hyperscaler weakness this week: Intel's record crash, Amazon's $33.5 billion cash burn and Alphabet's worst day ever. No EPS or revenue figures with basis or timing are given.

geopolitical: US midterm elections on Tuesday: all 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats. Trump approval is about 38%. Polymarket has Democrats at 94% for the House, and the Senate is harder.
A Democratic Congress could bring more federal attention to regulating the AI buildout. Trump holds the veto and has promised to 'veto everything'.

Goldman is cited (ZeroHedge, Oct 18) warning that higher yields are starting to break things, with the biggest crack in AI debt.

tension_points.theme: AI crowding-out and Treasury long end
tension_points.bull_case: Natixis argues a Democratic sweep could raise regulatory attention on the AI buildout, so AI issuance and lending could come in below market expectations. That would give relief to the long end after real yields reached 2007-2008 levels.
tension_points.bear_case: Trump holds the veto pen, has promised to 'veto everything' and supports the AI buildout, so no major federal legislation is expected. Market expectations are for AI activity to accelerate next year, and the Democratic agenda only takes shape into 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: AI-related issuance, lending and capex accelerate next year as the market expects, with the Fed hiking in December.

tension_points.bull_case: Natixis expects unchanged auction sizes and an ongoing message of flexibility.
tension_points.bear_case: Citi expects Bessent to cut 20Y and 30Y auction sizes and possibly end the 20Y, because AI is taking the pension bid.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Wednesday's refunding announcement settles whether auction sizes are unchanged or cut.
